A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Partial Model Collapse (PMC) research. All 23 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TOFU unlearning experiments, token-probability and multiple-choice analyses, ablations, and categorical and Gaussian-mixture simulations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and additionally reports sampling/prefilling attacks and ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy and MMLU evaluations.

M1.justification: The practical reward changes from similarity to ground-truth forget answers in v1 Section 6 to similarity to original-model answers in v3 Section 5. This revises the response-selection input and its dependence on ground truth, while the sampling, preference selection and weighted retain/forget loss remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v3 adds general reasoning and knowledge coverage through ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy and MMLU (Appendix A.1), and introduces adversarial prefilling conditions (Section 5.3). The existing TOFU, paraphrased-forget, world-facts, real-authors, wikitext, multiple-choice and synthetic-distribution coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The principal TOFU comparator suite remains GA, GD, NPO, SimNPO and IDK. However, v3 Appendix B.2 adds a timing comparison against the other unlearning methods, reporting 20–30 minute runtimes, whereas v1 Table 4 reports PMC timings alone. The new attack experiment reuses existing comparators.

E3.justification: v3 adds a robustness protocol that samples 100 responses per forget question, takes the maximum ROUGE-L score and averages these maxima across questions, with and without the prefix 'The answer is:'. Appendix B.5 specifies 20-epoch Llama training and attack sampling at temperature 0.9 and top-p 0.95. Existing TOFU splits, greedy metrics and grid-search settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.3 and Figure 6 test whether forgotten answers can be recovered through repeated sampling and forced prefilling, exposing IDK's vulnerability and comparing it with PMC and NPO. This adds a substantive robustness investigation. Existing hyperparameter ablations, probability-leakage analyses and categorical/Gaussian-mixture demonstrations are retained.

E5.justification: Five-seed averaging and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain the established practice, including for the new utility results. Runtime reporting changes from mean, minimum, maximum and standard deviation across 500 grid-search experiments in v1 to averages with ± values over five runs in v3. This changes the statistical summary without establishing an increase in experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: v3 adds attack-leakage findings and benchmark scores; new Table 1 reports Phi-1.5 ARC-Easy scores of 0.7622 for the base model and 0.6891 for PMC. It replaces v1's grid-search mean unlearning times of 4:49:20 and 7:24:30 with H100 summaries of 40 ± 2 and 30 ± 1 minutes, respectively; these differing reporting scopes do not establish a comparable speedup. Existing TOFU plots and fine-tuning scores are retained.

T1.justification: v1 Corollary 3 becomes v3 Theorem 1 and explicitly adds absence of function approximation errors to its assumptions. Its convergence statement and proof otherwise remain substantially unchanged. The categorical arguments and general-distribution Theorem 2 are retained, with the latter's main-text exposition moved to Appendix D.

C1.justification: The central collapse-based unlearning, convergence and utility claims remain. v3's abstract and introduction expand the claimed advantages from two to three by adding sampling/prefilling robustness, and the paper broadens its privacy emphasis from avoiding targets in the objective to operating without access to ground-truth forget answers.

C2.justification: v3 interprets IDK's failure under prefilling as superficial suppression and discusses applicability when original private data is unavailable or restricted. It also characterizes the new benchmark utility losses as minimal and the revised runtimes as practically reasonable. These are substantive additions to interpretation; the existing sampling-cost and evaluation limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.5 documents attack-model training and generation hyperparameters. Runtime documentation is revised to identify H100 timings, while v1's detailed grid-search runtime distribution and separate evaluation timings disappear. Existing fine-tuning settings, search spaces, ablation settings, multiple-choice templates and code-access disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Liu et al. (2025), Krishnan et al. (2025) and ARC/MMLU references, while trimming classification-related citations and removing Kuo et al. (2025) and Thaker et al. (2025). It additionally positions PMC as the first approach robust across both evaluated attack settings. The central positioning connecting model collapse and unlearning remains.

P1.justification: The method narrative is substantially reorganized: practical LLM unlearning becomes Section 4.3, the general-distribution exposition moves to Appendix D, and Gaussian-mixture demonstrations move to Appendix C. v3 also rewrites the preliminaries and motivation, expands explanations of conditional collapse, condenses ablation discussion and reorganizes Appendix B.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned around an explicit question-answer example and comparison with prior methods. v3 adds attack Figure 6 and utility Table 1, removes the old runtime table, recolors Figure 4 and relocates appendix displays. Most existing experimental plots and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The new attack tests directly investigate recovery of ostensibly forgotten answers, strengthening v1's greedy-output and probability-based evidence, while broader utility measurements make preservation claims more assessable. The reward revision also better supports ground-truth independence. These gains are tempered by the underqualified 'minimal to negligible' utility claim despite Phi-1.5's ARC-Easy decline from 0.7622 to 0.6891, and by replacing detailed runtime statistics with a less specified, non-comparable timing summary.
